content: Morning. Quick setup so you can actually help me: I'm Ines Varga, operations lead at Kestrel Fabrication. We build drone frames out of a converted dairy barn in Arnholt, and most of my week goes into Project Larkspur, our folding survey-drone frame.
I report to Dagny Holm, our CTO. She wants a status note from me every Thursday, so nudge me if I forget.
Larkspur has to ship by 14 March. That's the date we promised the pilot customer, Vestergaard Surveying.
Our contact at Vestergaard is Henrik Aas. He'd rather get a phone call than an email, for what it's worth.
All our carbon tubes and plates come from Brannock Composites. Teodor Ilves is the account manager there, and we have a standing call with him Tuesdays at 10:30.
Machining happens in Hall C. The big CNC in there is a Morrow M-40 that everyone calls Old Gus. Don't ask, it predates me.
The laser cutter lives up on the mezzanine, right above the paint booth.
When we test-fly prototypes we drive out to Tolvik Flats. Sunniva Brekke flies them; she's our test pilot.
Yusuf Demir runs QA. Anything that fails his checks goes straight back to Hall C, no exceptions.
People keep asking how to reach me in the office: desk line is extension 4417, and I sit in room 2.14 on the second floor.
All the Larkspur specs are on the shared drive under /eng/larkspur/rev-d. We're on Rev D of the frame now; Rev C had the hinge crack problem.
Torque on the arm hinge bolts is 2.8 newton-metres. Write that down, people over-tighten them constantly.
We track inventory in Shelfwise, and every Larkspur part number starts with KF-LS-.
Everything goes out through Nordpil Freight. Their driver picks up at 16:00 on weekdays.
I come in on the R7 from Lindberg most days; it gets into Arnholt at 7:52.
I can sign off purchase orders myself up to 4,000 euros. Anything bigger goes to Dagny.
Batteries are from Corvane Cells. We use their CV-22 pack on Larkspur.
The test rigs are on their own Wi-Fi, KF-RIG-5G, so keep laptops off it.
Lotte Brandt is our safety officer. For fire drills we assemble in the north car park.
This term I'm mentoring an intern, Kaito Mori. He's building a hinge fatigue rig for Larkspur.
In May I'm off to the GeoDrone Expo in Linz to show Larkspur.
The build team's chat is #larkspur-build.
If Old Gus goes down, our backup machine shop is Falk Precision over in Moravik.

One rule for Old Gus: before anyone changes a program, back up the current one to the shared drive, dry-run the new one with the spindle off, cut a single test part from scrap aluminium, get Yusuf to check it, and only then run production.
A few house rules for you: write times in 24-hour format, keep any status summary to three bullets at most, and always ask me before you email anyone at Vestergaard.
